items.q: Find the determinant of [[-3, 4], [-3, 1]].
items.s: For an array of order two the number is (-3)(1) - (4)(-3) = 9.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[6, 5, 3], [3, 7, 5], [0, 0, 0]].
items.s: The last row is entirely zero, so expanding along it gives a total of 0.

items.q: The reduced form of an array with 5 rows and five columns has 3 rows that are not entirely zero, all the other rows being zero. State its rank.
items.s: The rank is the count of rows that are not entirely zero in the reduced form, which is 3.

items.q: State the dimension of the space of all arrays with 2 rows and 4 columns under the usual entry by entry operations.
items.s: Every entry may be chosen freely, so the dimension is 2 x 4 = 8.

items.q: A space has a basis containing 5 members. State how many members every other basis of the same space must contain.
items.s: All bases of one space share the same count, so every other basis also contains 5 members.

items.q: An array of order two has eigenvalues 0 and 4. State its trace.
items.s: The trace equals the total of the eigenvalues, which is 4.

items.q: Under the usual rule the number assigned to the members (-4, 1, 1) and (3, 2, -3) is the sum of the products of matching coordinates. Find that number.
items.s: Multiplying matching coordinates and adding gives -13.

items.q: Given A = [[8, -4, 1], [3, 7, 7]], find the entry in row 2 and column 2 of the transpose of A.
items.s: The transpose writes rows as columns, so this entry is the one in row 2 and column 2 of A, namely 7.

items.q: Given A = [[2, 2], [6, -6]] and I the identity array of order two, find the top left entry of A + 3 I.
items.s: Scaling the identity changes only the diagonal, so the top left entry is 2 + 3 = 5.
The product is diagonal with entries 72, 45 and 12, so its trace is 129.

items.q: The array [[4, 0], [0, 6]] is multiplied on the left by [[1, 1], [0, 1]]. Find the top left entry of the product.
items.s: Only the diagonal entries survive the multiplication on the left by a unit triangular array, so the top left entry is 4.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[5, 4, 4], [0, 4, 0], [0, 2, 2]].
items.s: Expanding along the first column leaves 5 times the order two number 4 x 2, giving 40.

items.q: An array A of order two has determinant -7. Find the determinant of 2A.
items.s: Scaling both rows multiplies the number by 2^2 = 4, so the answer is 4 x -7 = -28.

items.q: Find the determinant of the upper triangular array [[4, 7, 2], [0, 3, 5], [0, 0, 4]].
items.s: For a triangular array the number is the product of the diagonal entries, here 4 x 3 x 4 = 48.

items.q: Two square arrays A and B of the same order have determinants 3 and 7. Find the determinant of AB.
items.s: The number attached to a product is the product of the two numbers, so it is 3 x 7 = 21.

items.q: In the array [[4, -3, 4], [4, 3, 3], [2, 2, 3]] find the cofactor of the entry in row one and column three.
items.s: Deleting row one and column three leaves the order two number (3)(3) - (3)(2) = 3, and the sign for that position is minus, so the cofactor is -3.

items.q: Find the top left entry of the inverse of [[4, 2], [1, 2]].
items.s: The determinant is 6, and the top left entry of the undoing array is 2/6 = 0.3333.

items.q: Find the bottom left entry of the inverse of [[1, 1], [1, 4]].
items.s: The bottom left entry of the undoing array is minus the lower left entry divided by the determinant 3, giving -0.3333.

items.q: An array of order two has determinant -4. Find the determinant of its inverse.
items.s: The number attached to the undoing array is the reciprocal of -4, which is -0.25.

items.q: Two nonsingular arrays A and B of order 3 are multiplied. State the position, written as 1 if on the left and 2 if on the right, of the factor that supplies the undoing of AB when that undoing is written as a product of the two undoings.
items.s: The undoing of AB is the undoing of B followed by the undoing of A, so the factor supplying A sits on the left, recorded as 1.

items.q: The system 3x + 5y = 4 and 4x + 2y = 7 has coefficient array [[3, 5], [4, 2]]. State the number of solutions it has.
items.s: The determinant of the coefficient array is -14, which is nonzero, so the system has exactly one solution.

items.q: Solve the system 3x + 2y = 27 and 1x + 3y = 23. State the value of x.
items.s: The determinant of the coefficient array is 7, and solving gives x = 5 and y = 6, so the value asked for is 5.

items.q: A homogeneous system of three conditions in three unknowns has coefficient array of determinant 2. State the number of unknowns that are free to take nonzero values in a nonzero solution.
items.s: With a nonzero determinant the only solution is the trivial one, so no unknown is free, recorded as 0.

items.q: An array has 5 columns and its reduced form has 2 rows that are not entirely zero. State its nullity.
items.s: Nullity is the count of columns without a leading entry, that is 5 - 2 = 3.

items.q: An array has 3 rows and 6 columns. State the largest value its rank can take.
items.s: The rank cannot exceed the smaller of the two counts, which here is 3.

items.q: State the dimension of the space of all polynomials of degree at most 4 together with the zero polynomial.
items.s: A basis is 1, x, and so on up to x^4, which is 5 members.

items.q: In the space of all ordered lists of 4 real numbers, consider the part made up of the lists whose first coordinate equals 3 times their second. State the dimension of that part.
items.s: One condition is imposed on 4 freely chosen coordinates, so the part has dimension 4 - 1 = 3.

items.q: A part of a space is made up of all members whose first coordinate equals 3 times their second. State 1 if that part is closed under addition and 0 if it is not.
items.s: Adding two members that each satisfy the condition gives a member that also satisfies it, so the part is closed, recorded as 1.

items.q: The list (6, 6) is expressed in the basis whose first member is (2, 0) and second member is (0, 2). Find its first coordinate in that basis.
items.s: The first basis member carries only a first coordinate, so the first coordinate is 6 divided by 2, which is 3.

items.q: Two members of the plane have coordinates (1, 5) and (3, 15). State 1 if they are independent and 0 if they are dependent.
items.s: The second member is 3 times the first, so the pair is dependent and the answer is 0.

items.q: A collection of 3 members of the space of ordered lists of 2 real numbers is given. State the largest number of them that can be independent.
items.s: At most 2 members of that space can be independent, so among 3 members the largest independent selection has 2.

items.q: An array of order two has eigenvalues 3 and 5. State its determinant.
items.s: The determinant equals the product of the eigenvalues, which is 15.

items.q: Find the sum of the two eigenvalues of [[6, 3], [-3, -4]].
items.s: The sum of the eigenvalues equals the trace, which is 6 + -4 = 2.

items.q: The characteristic expression of an array of order two is L^2 - 11L + 30, where L stands for the unknown number. State the smaller of the two values it produces when set to zero.
items.s: The expression has roots 5 and 6, so the smaller is 5.

items.q: Find the product of the two eigenvalues of [[-1, -2], [1, -3]].
items.s: The product of the eigenvalues equals the determinant, which is (-1)(-3) - (-2)(1) = 5.

items.q: The array [[5, 0], [0, 7]] acts on the column (1, 0). State the factor by which the result is a multiple of that column.
items.s: The first coordinate is multiplied by 5 while the second stays zero, so the factor is 5.

items.q: A diagonal array of order two has both diagonal entries equal to 3. Find the trace of its 5th power.
items.s: Each diagonal entry of the power is 3^5 = 243, so the trace is twice that, 486.

items.q: An array of order two has eigenvalues 3 and 4. Find the determinant of its 2nd power.
items.s: The eigenvalues of the power are 3^2 and 4^2, so the determinant is their product 144.

items.q: An array of order 4 has 4 eigenvalues all different from one another. State how many independent members belonging to those values exist in total.
items.s: Distinct values of an array of order 4 supply one independent member each, so 4 in all.

items.q: Two similar arrays of order three both have trace 2. State the trace of the second of them after either is multiplied on the left by a nonsingular array and on the right by the undoing of that array.
items.s: Similar arrays share the same trace, so the value remains 2.

items.q: Find the norm of the member (2, 6, 9) under the usual rule.
items.s: The norm is the square root of the sum of squares 121, which is 11.

items.q: The member (4, 2, 4) lies along the direction (2, 1, 2). Find the scalar multiple that expresses it in terms of that direction.
items.s: Matching coordinates are all 2 times as large, so the multiple is 2.

items.q: State the number assigned by the usual rule to the members (3, 3, 0) and (3, -3, 0).
items.s: The products of matching coordinates are 9 and -9, whose total is 0.

items.q: A member has length 3 and another has length 5. Find the largest value their pairing number under the usual rule can take, to three decimal places.
items.s: By the Cauchy inequality the pairing number never exceeds the product of the lengths, 3 x 5 = 15.

items.q: Given A = [[6, -1], [5, 6]] and B = [[-4, 4], [4, -5]], find the entry in row 2 and column 2 of AB.
items.s: Row 2 of A is (5, 6) and column 2 of B is (4, -5), so the entry is 5 x 4 + 6 x -5 = -10.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[-1, 2], [2, -4]].
items.s: For an array of order two the number is (-1)(-4) - (2)(2) = 0.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[5, 2, 3], [2, 6, 5], [0, 0, 0]].
items.s: The last row is entirely zero, so expanding along it gives a total of 0.

items.q: A system with coefficient array [[3, 1], [1, 3]] has right hand column (7, 9). Using the determinant method, find the first unknown.
items.s: The first unknown is (7 x 3 - 1 x 9)/8 = 1.5.

items.q: The reduced form of an array with 4 rows and five columns has 3 rows that are not entirely zero, all the other rows being zero. State its rank.
items.s: The rank is the count of rows that are not entirely zero in the reduced form, which is 3.

items.q: A space has a basis containing 4 members. State how many members every other basis of the same space must contain.
items.s: All bases of one space share the same count, so every other basis also contains 4 members.

items.q: An array of order two has eigenvalues -4 and 3. State its trace.
items.s: The trace equals the total of the eigenvalues, which is -1.

items.q: Under the usual rule the number assigned to the members (0, 2, 1) and (5, -4, 4) is the sum of the products of matching coordinates. Find that number.
items.s: Multiplying matching coordinates and adding gives -4.

items.q: Given A = [[6, -4, -3], [4, -4, -4]], find the entry in row 1 and column 1 of the transpose of A.
items.s: The transpose writes rows as columns, so this entry is the one in row 1 and column 1 of A, namely 6.

items.q: Given A = [[-6, 0], [3, -4]] and I the identity array of order two, find the top left entry of A - 2 I.
items.s: Scaling the identity changes only the diagonal, so the top left entry is -6 - 2 = -8.
The product is diagonal with entries 20, 32 and 10, so its trace is 62.

items.q: The array [[3, 0], [0, 5]] is multiplied on the left by [[1, 1], [0, 1]]. Find the top left entry of the product.
items.s: Only the diagonal entries survive the multiplication on the left by a unit triangular array, so the top left entry is 3.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[5, 3, 4], [0, 3, 0], [0, 1, 2]].
items.s: Expanding along the first column leaves 5 times the order two number 3 x 2, giving 30.

items.q: An array A of order two has determinant 4. Find the determinant of 4A.
items.s: Scaling both rows multiplies the number by 4^2 = 16, so the answer is 16 x 4 = 64.

items.q: Find the determinant of the upper triangular array [[2, 7, 2], [0, 2, 5], [0, 0, 3]].
items.s: For a triangular array the number is the product of the diagonal entries, here 2 x 2 x 3 = 12.

items.q: Two square arrays A and B of the same order have determinants 6 and 7. Find the determinant of AB.
items.s: The number attached to a product is the product of the two numbers, so it is 6 x 7 = 42.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines spectrum?
o: how many times a value appears as a root of the expression in a single symbol
an array with the same count of rows as of columns
the whole collection of values attached to an array
the count of rows written together with the count of columns
items.s: spectrum: the whole collection of values attached to an array. The other options describe algebraic multiplicity, order of a matrix, square matrix.

items.q: Which of the following best describes identity matrix?
o: the part of a member lying along a chosen direction
how many times a value appears as a root of the expression in a single symbol
the situation in which some combination with not all scalars zero gives the zero member
a square one with ones on the leading diagonal and zeros everywhere else
items.s: identity matrix: a square one with ones on the leading diagonal and zeros everywhere else. The other options describe orthogonal projection, linear dependence, algebraic multiplicity.

items.q: singular matrix may be defined as
o: one of the three allowed changes: swapping rows, scaling a row, or adding a multiple of a row to another
the situation in which only the all zero choice of scalars gives the zero member
the statement that the assigned number of a pair never exceeds the product of the two lengths
a square one whose attached single number is zero
items.s: singular matrix: a square one whose attached single number is zero. The other options describe linear independence, Cauchy inequality, elementary row operation.

items.q: Which term is described by “the single number attached to a square array that tells whether it can be undone”?
o: vanishing row case
cofactor
triangular matrix
determinant
items.s: determinant is the single number attached to a square array that tells whether it can be undone.

items.q: The statement “the situation in which two rows of a square array are equal so that its number is zero” describes which of the following?
o: triangular matrix
vanishing row case
cofactor expansion
determinant
items.s: vanishing row case is the situation in which two rows of a square array are equal so that its number is zero.

items.q: Which term is described by “the array whose columns are the old coordinates of the newly chosen members”?
o: exchange lemma
change of basis matrix
standard basis
basis
items.s: change of basis matrix is the array whose columns are the old coordinates of the newly chosen members.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines singular matrix?
o: one of the three allowed changes: swapping rows, scaling a row, or adding a multiple of a row to another
a nonzero member that a given array merely stretches or reverses
the array of coefficients written beside the column of right hand values
a square one whose attached single number is zero
items.s: singular matrix: a square one whose attached single number is zero. The other options describe eigenvector, augmented matrix, elementary row operation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes invertibility condition?
o: the requirement that the single number attached to a square array is not zero
the unique element that leaves every element unchanged when added to it
the statement that a member of a spanning collection can be swapped for an outside member and still span
the collection of unit lists each having one in a single position and zeros elsewhere
items.s: invertibility condition: the requirement that the single number attached to a square array is not zero. The other options describe zero member, exchange lemma, standard basis.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines cofactor expansion?
o: the list of scalars that expresses a member in terms of a chosen basis
the writing of the whole number as a sum of entries of one row each multiplied by its signed smaller value
an unknown whose value may be chosen at will once the others are fixed
the single number attached to a square array that tells whether it can be undone
items.s: cofactor expansion: the writing of the whole number as a sum of entries of one row each multiplied by its signed smaller value. The other options describe determinant, free variable, coordinate vector.

items.q: Which of the following best describes involutory matrix?
o: the situation in which two rows of a square array are equal so that its number is zero
a part of a space that is itself a space under the same two operations
a square one in which every entry on one side of the leading diagonal is zero
a square one that is its own undoing array
items.s: involutory matrix: a square one that is its own undoing array. The other options describe vanishing row case, triangular matrix, subspace.

items.q: Which term is described by “the writing of an array as a sandwich of a basis array and the undoing of that array around a diagonal one”?
o: diagonalisation
matrix power
defective matrix
invariant direction
items.s: diagonalisation is the writing of an array as a sandwich of a basis array and the undoing of that array around a diagonal one.

items.q: Which term is described by “a nonzero member that a given array merely stretches or reverses”?
o: geometric multiplicity
characteristic equation
eigenvector
algebraic multiplicity
items.s: eigenvector is a nonzero member that a given array merely stretches or reverses.

items.q: orthogonal projection may be defined as
o: the result of applying an array to itself a stated number of times
the part of a member lying along a chosen direction
a square one with ones on the leading diagonal and zeros everywhere else
the list of scalars that expresses a member in terms of a chosen basis
items.s: orthogonal projection: the part of a member lying along a chosen direction. The other options describe identity matrix, coordinate vector, matrix power.

items.q: The statement “the situation in which some combination with not all scalars zero gives the zero member” describes which of the following?
o: maximal independent set
basis
change of basis matrix
linear dependence
items.s: linear dependence is the situation in which some combination with not all scalars zero gives the zero member.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines inconsistent system?
o: a square one whose entries away from the leading diagonal are all zero
a set of conditions that no set of values can satisfy together
an independent collection that also produces every member of the space
the part of a member lying along a chosen direction
items.s: inconsistent system: a set of conditions that no set of values can satisfy together. The other options describe diagonal matrix, basis, orthogonal projection.

items.q: Which of the following best describes matrix power?
o: the statement that the undoing array equals the transposed signed values divided by the single number
the result of applying an array to itself a stated number of times
a set of unit members that are pairwise assigned the number zero
a nonzero member that a given array merely stretches or reverses
items.s: matrix power: the result of applying an array to itself a stated number of times. The other options describe orthonormal collection, inverse formula, eigenvector.

items.q: Which term is described by “the part of a member lying along a chosen direction”?
o: orthogonal complement
orthogonal projection
orthonormal collection
Gram determinant
items.s: orthogonal projection is the part of a member lying along a chosen direction.

items.q: Which term is described by “two arrays whose inner counts agree, so that they may be multiplied in that stated sequence”?
o: conformable pair
skew symmetric matrix
square matrix
identity matrix
items.s: conformable pair is two arrays whose inner counts agree, so that they may be multiplied in that stated sequence.

items.q: Which term is described by “the whole collection of values attached to an array”?
o: characteristic equation
eigenvalue
characteristic polynomial
spectrum
items.s: spectrum is the whole collection of values attached to an array.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines inverse of a product?
o: the reversal rule that undoing a chain of factors gives the individual undoings in the opposite order
a part of a space that is itself a space under the same two operations
the count of columns without a leading entry in the simplified form
the count of independent members belonging to one value
items.s: inverse of a product: the reversal rule that undoing a chain of factors gives the individual undoings in the opposite order. The other options describe geometric multiplicity, nullity, subspace.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines inner product?
o: a collection whose combinations produce every member of the space
a line through the origin that a given array maps onto itself
a square one that is its own undoing array
a rule assigning a number to each ordered pair of members, symmetric and positive on each member with itself
items.s: inner product: a rule assigning a number to each ordered pair of members, symmetric and positive on each member with itself. The other options describe spanning set, invariant direction, involutory matrix.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines algebraic multiplicity?
o: the set of values in which every unknown is zero
the situation in which two rows of a square array are equal so that its number is zero
how many times a value appears as a root of the expression in a single symbol
a line through the origin that a given array maps onto itself
items.s: algebraic multiplicity: how many times a value appears as a root of the expression in a single symbol. The other options describe trivial solution, invariant direction, vanishing row case.

items.q: Which of the following best describes geometric multiplicity?
o: the single set of values satisfying a consistent set of conditions
the count of independent members belonging to one value
the collection of unit lists each having one in a single position and zeros elsewhere
the array whose columns are the old coordinates of the newly chosen members
items.s: geometric multiplicity: the count of independent members belonging to one value. The other options describe change of basis matrix, unique solution, standard basis.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines column space.
o: the collection of unit lists each having one in a single position and zeros elsewhere
two arrays whose inner counts agree, so that they may be multiplied in that stated sequence
a collection that is independent and cannot be enlarged without losing that property
the set of all combinations of the columns of an array
items.s: column space: the set of all combinations of the columns of an array. The other options describe standard basis, conformable pair, maximal independent set.

items.q: Which term is described by “the array of signed smaller values of a square one, written with rows and columns interchanged”?
o: left cancellation
invertibility condition
adjugate
inverse formula
items.s: adjugate is the array of signed smaller values of a square one, written with rows and columns interchanged.

items.q: Which of the following best describes null matrix?
o: a simplified array in which each leading entry is one and is the only nonzero entry in its column
one in which every entry is zero
the single set of values satisfying a consistent set of conditions
the requirement that the single number attached to a square array is not zero
items.s: null matrix: one in which every entry is zero. The other options describe reduced row echelon form, invertibility condition, unique solution.

items.q: closure under addition may be defined as
o: the part formed by the zero member together with all members belonging to one value
an array with the same count of rows as of columns
the property that combining any two members of the set stays inside it
the set of all combinations of the columns of an array
items.s: closure under addition: the property that combining any two members of the set stays inside it. The other options describe column space, eigenspace, square matrix.

items.q: Which of the following best describes algebraic multiplicity?
o: how many times a value appears as a root of the expression in a single symbol
the array of signed smaller values of a square one, written with rows and columns interchanged
the collection of unit lists each having one in a single position and zeros elsewhere
the part formed by the zero member together with all members belonging to one value
items.s: algebraic multiplicity: how many times a value appears as a root of the expression in a single symbol. The other options describe eigenspace, adjugate, standard basis.

items.q: The statement “a square one in which every entry on one side of the leading diagonal is zero” describes which of the following?
o: cofactor expansion
triangular matrix
nonsingular matrix
vanishing row case
items.s: triangular matrix is a square one in which every entry on one side of the leading diagonal is zero.

items.q: The statement “the reversal rule that undoing a chain of factors gives the individual undoings in the opposite order” describes which of the following?
o: involutory matrix
inverse of a product
left cancellation
inverse
items.s: inverse of a product is the reversal rule that undoing a chain of factors gives the individual undoings in the opposite order.

items.q: linear combination may be defined as
o: a square one whose entries away from the leading diagonal are all zero
a sum of scalar multiples of a collection of members
the array of signed smaller values of a square one, written with rows and columns interchanged
the number formed from all the pairwise assigned numbers of a collection, testing independence
items.s: linear combination: a sum of scalar multiples of a collection of members. The other options describe adjugate, Gram determinant, diagonal matrix.

items.q: determinant may be defined as
o: the single number attached to a square array that tells whether it can be undone
a number for which some nonzero member is carried to a multiple of itself
the array which, multiplied by the given one on either side, gives the identity
the smaller number of a chosen entry multiplied by plus or minus one according to its position
items.s: determinant: the single number attached to a square array that tells whether it can be undone. The other options describe inverse, eigenvalue, cofactor.

items.q: orthogonal matrix may be defined as
o: the expression in a single symbol obtained by subtracting that symbol from the diagonal before taking the attached number
the single number attached to a square array that tells whether it can be undone
a square one whose rows and columns interchanged array is also its undoing array
the writing of an array as a sandwich of a basis array and the undoing of that array around a diagonal one
items.s: orthogonal matrix: a square one whose rows and columns interchanged array is also its undoing array. The other options describe determinant, characteristic polynomial, diagonalisation.

items.q: The statement “two arrays related by an undoing array on one side and the array itself on the other” describes which of the following?
o: matrix power
defective matrix
similar matrices
invariant direction
items.s: similar matrices is two arrays related by an undoing array on one side and the array itself on the other.

items.q: The statement “a square one that is unchanged when its rows and columns are interchanged” describes which of the following?
o: symmetric matrix
transpose
skew symmetric matrix
null matrix
items.s: symmetric matrix is a square one that is unchanged when its rows and columns are interchanged.

items.q: skew symmetric matrix may be defined as
o: a square one that becomes the negative of itself when its rows and columns are interchanged
a line through the origin that a given array maps onto itself
a nonzero member that a given array merely stretches or reverses
the smaller number left after deleting the row and the column that contain a chosen entry
items.s: skew symmetric matrix: a square one that becomes the negative of itself when its rows and columns are interchanged. The other options describe minor, invariant direction, eigenvector.

items.q: Which term is described by “a square one that is its own undoing array”?
o: invertibility condition
involutory matrix
inverse of a product
inverse formula
items.s: involutory matrix is a square one that is its own undoing array.

items.q: Which of the following best describes pivot?
o: the part of a member lying along a chosen direction
the count of columns without a leading entry in the simplified form
the total of the entries on the leading diagonal
the first nonzero entry in a row of a simplified array, used to clear the entries beneath it
items.s: pivot: the first nonzero entry in a row of a simplified array, used to clear the entries beneath it. The other options describe nullity, orthogonal projection, trace.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines similar matrices?
o: the set of values in which every unknown is zero
the reversal rule that undoing a chain of factors gives the individual undoings in the opposite order
two arrays related by an undoing array on one side and the array itself on the other
the writing of the whole number as a sum of entries of one row each multiplied by its signed smaller value
items.s: similar matrices: two arrays related by an undoing array on one side and the array itself on the other. The other options describe inverse of a product, trivial solution, cofactor expansion.

items.q: Which of the following best describes triangular matrix?
o: a square one in which every entry on one side of the leading diagonal is zero
the writing of the whole number as a sum of entries of one row each multiplied by its signed smaller value
a line through the origin that a given array maps onto itself
everything that is assigned the number zero with every member of a stated part
items.s: triangular matrix: a square one in which every entry on one side of the leading diagonal is zero. The other options describe invariant direction, orthogonal complement, cofactor expansion.

items.q: Which of the following best describes inverse of a product?
o: the result of applying an array to itself a stated number of times
the reversal rule that undoing a chain of factors gives the individual undoings in the opposite order
the count of nonzero rows in the fully simplified form of an array
a number for which some nonzero member is carried to a multiple of itself
items.s: inverse of a product: the reversal rule that undoing a chain of factors gives the individual undoings in the opposite order. The other options describe matrix power, rank, eigenvalue.

items.q: Which of the following best describes symmetric matrix?
o: a square one that is unchanged when its rows and columns are interchanged
the result of applying an array to itself a stated number of times
the single number attached to a square array that tells whether it can be undone
a square one in which every entry on one side of the leading diagonal is zero
items.s: symmetric matrix: a square one that is unchanged when its rows and columns are interchanged. The other options describe triangular matrix, determinant, matrix power.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines linear combination?
o: the list of scalars that expresses a member in terms of a chosen basis
a square one that cannot be written in sandwich form because some value lacks enough members
a sum of scalar multiples of a collection of members
the setting to zero of the expression in a single symbol that arises from the diagonal subtraction
items.s: linear combination: a sum of scalar multiples of a collection of members. The other options describe coordinate vector, defective matrix, characteristic equation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes elementary row operation?
o: a square one whose entries away from the leading diagonal are all zero
the smaller number of a chosen entry multiplied by plus or minus one according to its position
one of the three allowed changes: swapping rows, scaling a row, or adding a multiple of a row to another
a square one whose rows and columns interchanged array is also its undoing array

the fact that having all values different guarantees an array can be written in sandwich form

the first nonzero entry in a row of a simplified array, used to clear the entries beneath it

two arrays related by an undoing array on one side and the array itself on the other
how many times a value appears as a root of the expression in a single symbol

the statement that the assigned number of a pair never exceeds the product of the two lengths
the list of scalars that expresses a member in terms of a chosen basis

the whole collection of values attached to an array
a simplified array in which each leading entry is one and is the only nonzero entry in its column
the count of members in any basis of the space

a collection whose combinations produce every member of the space

items.q: Find the determinant of [[3, -1, 5], [0, 3, 0], [0, 1, 2]].
items.s: Expanding along the first column leaves 3 times the order two number 3 x 2, giving 18.

items.q: Find the top left entry of the inverse of [[4, 3], [2, 3]].
items.s: The determinant is 6, and the top left entry of the undoing array is 3/6 = 0.5.

items.q: The system 2x + 4y = 4 and 1x + 3y = 7 has coefficient array [[2, 4], [1, 3]]. State the number of solutions it has.
items.s: The determinant of the coefficient array is 2, which is nonzero, so the system has exactly one solution = 1.

items.q: An array has 4 columns and its reduced form has 2 rows that are not entirely zero. State its nullity.
items.s: Nullity is the count of columns without a leading entry, that is 4 - 2 = 2.

items.q: State the dimension of the space of all polynomials of degree at most 3 together with the zero polynomial.
items.s: A basis is 1, x, and so on up to x^3, which is 4 members.

items.q: The list (9, 3) is expressed in the basis whose first member is (3, 0) and second member is (0, 1). Find its first coordinate in that basis.
items.s: The first basis member carries only a first coordinate, so the first coordinate is 9 divided by 3, which is 3.

items.q: An array of order two has eigenvalues 4 and 2. State its determinant.
items.s: The determinant equals the product of the eigenvalues, which is 8.

items.q: Find the sum of the two eigenvalues of [[-1, 3], [-1, -2]].
items.s: The sum of the eigenvalues equals the trace, which is -1 + -2 = -3.

items.q: A diagonal array of order two has both diagonal entries equal to 2. Find the trace of its 4th power.
items.s: Each diagonal entry of the power is 2^4 = 16, so the trace is twice that, 32.

items.q: Find the norm of the member (3, 4, 12) under the usual rule.
items.s: The norm is the square root of the sum of squares 169, which is 13.

items.q: Given A = [[5, 4], [-6, 3]] and B = [[4, 1], [0, -1]], find the entry in row 1 and column 1 of AB.
items.s: Row 1 of A is (5, 4) and column 1 of B is (4, 0), so the entry is 5 x 4 + 4 x 0 = 20.

items.q: Given A = [[-4, -6], [8, -5]] and I the identity array of order two, find the top left entry of A + 2 I.
items.s: Scaling the identity changes only the diagonal, so the top left entry is -4 + 2 = -2.
The product is diagonal with entries 30, 20 and 12, so its trace is 62.

items.q: The array [[2, 0], [0, 4]] is multiplied on the left by [[1, 1], [0, 1]]. Find the top left entry of the product.
items.s: Only the diagonal entries survive the multiplication on the left by a unit triangular array, so the top left entry is 2.

items.q: An array A of order two has determinant -7. Find the determinant of 4A.
items.s: Scaling both rows multiplies the number by 4^2 = 16, so the answer is 16 x -7 = -112.

items.q: Find the determinant of the upper triangular array [[6, 7, 2], [0, 4, 5], [0, 0, 2]].
items.s: For a triangular array the number is the product of the diagonal entries, here 6 x 4 x 2 = 48.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[4, 4, 3], [7, 5, 5], [0, 0, 0]].
items.s: The last row is entirely zero, so expanding along it gives a total of 0.

items.q: In the array [[4, 1, 2], [-1, 4, -1], [3, 1, 3]] find the cofactor of the entry in row one and column three.
items.s: Deleting row one and column three leaves the order two number (4)(3) - (-1)(1) = 13, and the sign for that position is minus, so the cofactor is -13.

items.q: Find the bottom left entry of the inverse of [[2, 2], [4, 5]].
items.s: The bottom left entry of the undoing array is minus the lower left entry divided by the determinant 2, giving -2.

items.q: An array of order two has determinant -2. Find the determinant of its inverse.
items.s: The number attached to the undoing array is the reciprocal of -2, which is -0.5.

items.q: A system with coefficient array [[2, 3], [2, 1]] has right hand column (6, 6). Using the determinant method, find the first unknown.
items.s: The first unknown is (6 x 1 - 3 x 6)/-4 = 3.

items.q: Solve the system 3x + 2y = 14 and 1x + 3y = 7. State the value of y.
items.s: The determinant of the coefficient array is 7, and solving gives x = 4 and y = 1, so the value asked for is 1.

items.q: A homogeneous system of three conditions in three unknowns has coefficient array of determinant 4. State the number of unknowns that are free to take nonzero values in a nonzero solution.
items.s: With a nonzero determinant the only solution is the trivial one, so no unknown is free, recorded as 0.

items.q: State the dimension of the space of all arrays with 4 rows and 2 columns under the usual entry by entry operations.
items.s: Every entry may be chosen freely, so the dimension is 4 x 2 = 8.

items.q: In the space of all ordered lists of 3 real numbers, consider the part made up of the lists whose first coordinate equals 3 times their second. State the dimension of that part.
items.s: One condition is imposed on 3 freely chosen coordinates, so the part has dimension 3 - 1 = 2.

items.q: A part of a space is made up of all members whose first coordinate equals 5 times their second. State 1 if that part is closed under addition and 0 if it is not.
items.s: Adding two members that each satisfy the condition gives a member that also satisfies it, so the part is closed, recorded as 1.

items.q: A space has a basis containing 3 members. State how many members every other basis of the same space must contain.
items.s: All bases of one space share the same count, so every other basis also contains 3 members.

items.q: Two members of the plane have coordinates (5, 3) and (10, 6). State 1 if they are independent and 0 if they are dependent.
items.s: The second member is 2 times the first, so the pair is dependent and the answer is 0.

items.q: An array of order two has eigenvalues -1 and 5. State its trace.
items.s: The trace equals the total of the eigenvalues, which is 4.

items.q: The characteristic expression of an array of order two is L^2 - 8L + 12, where L stands for the unknown number. State the smaller of the two values it produces when set to zero.
items.s: The expression has roots 2 and 6, so the smaller is 2.

items.q: Find the product of the two eigenvalues of [[-4, -4], [0, 1]].
items.s: The product of the eigenvalues equals the determinant, which is (-4)(1) - (-4)(0) = -4.

items.q: An array of order two has eigenvalues 3 and 5. Find the determinant of its 3rd power.
items.s: The eigenvalues of the power are 3^3 and 5^3, so the determinant is their product 3375.

items.q: An array of order 3 has 3 eigenvalues all different from one another. State how many independent members belonging to those values exist in total.
items.s: Distinct values of an array of order 3 supply one independent member each, so 3 in all.

items.q: Two similar arrays of order three both have trace 9. State the trace of the second of them after either is multiplied on the left by a nonsingular array and on the right by the undoing of that array.
items.s: Similar arrays share the same trace, so the value remains 9.

items.q: Under the usual rule the number assigned to the members (-1, 1, 0) and (4, 2, 0) is the sum of the products of matching coordinates. Find that number.
items.s: Multiplying matching coordinates and adding gives -2.

items.q: The member (2, 4, 0) lies along the direction (1, 2, 0). Find the scalar multiple that expresses it in terms of that direction.
items.s: Matching coordinates are all 2 times as large, so the multiple is 2.

items.q: A member has length 9 and another has length 12. Find the largest value their pairing number under the usual rule can take, to three decimal places.
items.s: By the Cauchy inequality the pairing number never exceeds the product of the lengths, 9 x 12 = 108.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[1, -1, 1], [0, 4, 0], [0, -1, 2]].
items.s: Expanding along the first column leaves 1 times the order two number 4 x 2, giving 8.

items.q: Find the top left entry of the inverse of [[2, 2], [3, 4]].
items.s: The determinant is 2, and the top left entry of the undoing array is 4/2 = 2.

items.q: The system 3x + 4y = 4 and 2x + 2y = 7 has coefficient array [[3, 4], [2, 2]]. State the number of solutions it has.
items.s: The determinant of the coefficient array is -2, which is nonzero, so the system has exactly one solution = 1.

items.q: An array has 4 columns and its reduced form has 3 rows that are not entirely zero. State its nullity.
items.s: Nullity is the count of columns without a leading entry, that is 4 - 3 = 1.

items.q: The list (6, 6) is expressed in the basis whose first member is (3, 0) and second member is (0, 3). Find its first coordinate in that basis.
items.s: The first basis member carries only a first coordinate, so the first coordinate is 6 divided by 3, which is 2.

items.q: An array of order two has eigenvalues -3 and 2. State its determinant.
items.s: The determinant equals the product of the eigenvalues, which is -6.

items.q: Find the sum of the two eigenvalues of [[8, 3], [-5, -2]].
items.s: The sum of the eigenvalues equals the trace, which is 8 + -2 = 6.

items.q: Find the norm of the member (2, 3, 6) under the usual rule.
items.s: The norm is the square root of the sum of squares 49, which is 7.

items.q: Given A = [[-6, -5], [-1, 3]] and B = [[5, 5], [-2, -1]], find the entry in row 1 and column 1 of AB.
items.s: Row 1 of A is (-6, -5) and column 1 of B is (5, -2), so the entry is -6 x 5 + -5 x -2 = -20.

items.q: Given A = [[4, 0], [-3, 7]] and I the identity array of order two, find the top left entry of A + 3 I.
items.s: Scaling the identity changes only the diagonal, so the top left entry is 4 + 3 = 7.
The product is diagonal with entries 40, 56 and 36, so its trace is 132.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[-4, 0], [0, -3]].
items.s: For an array of order two the number is (-4)(-3) - (0)(0) = 12.

items.q: Find the determinant of the upper triangular array [[3, 7, 2], [0, 5, 5], [0, 0, 2]].
items.s: For a triangular array the number is the product of the diagonal entries, here 3 x 5 x 2 = 30.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[4, 7, 3], [4, 5, 5], [0, 0, 0]].
items.s: The last row is entirely zero, so expanding along it gives a total of 0.

items.q: Two square arrays A and B of the same order have determinants 5 and 4. Find the determinant of AB.
items.s: The number attached to a product is the product of the two numbers, so it is 5 x 4 = 20.

items.q: In the array [[2, -3, 2], [4, 2, 1], [4, 2, 3]] find the cofactor of the entry in row one and column three.
items.s: Deleting row one and column three leaves the order two number (2)(3) - (1)(2) = 4, and the sign for that position is minus, so the cofactor is -4.

items.q: Find the bottom left entry of the inverse of [[3, 1], [4, 4]].
items.s: The bottom left entry of the undoing array is minus the lower left entry divided by the determinant 8, giving -0.5.

items.q: Two nonsingular arrays A and B of order 2 are multiplied. State the position, written as 1 if on the left and 2 if on the right, of the factor that supplies the undoing of AB when that undoing is written as a product of the two undoings.
items.s: The undoing of AB is the undoing of B followed by the undoing of A, so the factor supplying A sits on the left, recorded as 1.

items.q: A system with coefficient array [[1, 4], [4, 4]] has right hand column (2, 4). Using the determinant method, find the first unknown.
items.s: The first unknown is (2 x 4 - 4 x 4)/-12 = 0.6667.

items.q: Solve the system 2x + 1y = 6 and 1x + 3y = 13. State the value of y.
items.s: The determinant of the coefficient array is 5, and solving gives x = 1 and y = 4, so the value asked for is 4.

items.q: An array has 4 rows and 6 columns. State the largest value its rank can take.
items.s: The rank cannot exceed the smaller of the two counts, which here is 4.

items.q: A part of a space is made up of all members whose first coordinate equals 2 times their second. State 1 if that part is closed under addition and 0 if it is not.
items.s: Adding two members that each satisfy the condition gives a member that also satisfies it, so the part is closed, recorded as 1.

items.q: Two members of the plane have coordinates (4, 1) and (12, 3). State 1 if they are independent and 0 if they are dependent.
items.s: The second member is 3 times the first, so the pair is dependent and the answer is 0.

basis

items.q: Given A = [[6, 0], [2, 6]] and B = [[-5, 4], [4, 6]], find the entry in row 1 and column 2 of AB.

items.q: An array has 6 columns and its reduced form has 2 rows that are not entirely zero. State its nullity.
items.s: Nullity is the count of columns without a leading entry, that is 6 - 2 = 4.

items.q: State the dimension of the space of all arrays with 3 rows and 3 columns under the usual entry by entry operations.
items.s: Every entry may be chosen freely, so the dimension is 3 x 3 = 9.

items.q: In the space of all ordered lists of 4 real numbers, consider the part made up of the lists whose first coordinate equals 4 times their second. State the dimension of that part.
items.s: One condition is imposed on 4 freely chosen coordinates, so the part has dimension 4 - 1 = 3.

items.q: The list (8, 2) is expressed in the basis whose first member is (4, 0) and second member is (0, 1). Find its first coordinate in that basis.
items.s: The first basis member carries only a first coordinate, so the first coordinate is 8 divided by 4, which is 2.

items.q: Two members of the plane have coordinates (2, 1) and (6, 3). State 1 if they are independent and 0 if they are dependent.
items.s: The second member is 3 times the first, so the pair is dependent and the answer is 0.

items.q: Find the sum of the two eigenvalues of [[-2, 1], [-2, -1]].
items.s: The sum of the eigenvalues equals the trace, which is -2 + -1 = -3.

items.q: The characteristic expression of an array of order two is L^2 - 5L + 6, where L stands for the unknown number. State the smaller of the two values it produces when set to zero.
items.s: The expression has roots 3 and 2, so the smaller is 2.

items.q: Find the product of the two eigenvalues of [[-5, -4], [0, -5]].
items.s: The product of the eigenvalues equals the determinant, which is (-5)(-5) - (-4)(0) = 25.

items.q: A diagonal array of order two has both diagonal entries equal to 3. Find the trace of its 3rd power.
items.s: Each diagonal entry of the power is 3^3 = 27, so the trace is twice that, 54.

items.q: An array of order two has eigenvalues 2 and 5. Find the determinant of its 3rd power.
items.s: The eigenvalues of the power are 2^3 and 5^3, so the determinant is their product 1000.

items.q: Under the usual rule the number assigned to the members (-2, 5, -1) and (-4, -3, -2) is the sum of the products of matching coordinates. Find that number.
items.s: Multiplying matching coordinates and adding gives -5.

items.q: Two square arrays A and B of the same order have determinants 6 and -3. Find the determinant of AB.
items.s: The number attached to a product is the product of the two numbers, so it is 6 x -3 = -18.

items.q: In the array [[2, 3, 1], [4, 4, -3], [3, 4, 3]] find the cofactor of the entry in row one and column three.
items.s: Deleting row one and column three leaves the order two number (4)(3) - (-3)(4) = 24, and the sign for that position is minus, so the cofactor is -24.

items.q: A collection of 4 members of the space of ordered lists of 3 real numbers is given. State the largest number of them that can be independent.
items.s: At most 3 members of that space can be independent, so among 4 members the largest independent selection has 3.

items.q: Two similar arrays of order three both have trace 10. State the trace of the second of them after either is multiplied on the left by a nonsingular array and on the right by the undoing of that array.
items.s: Similar arrays share the same trace, so the value remains 10.

items.q: State the number assigned by the usual rule to the members (1, 2, 0) and (2, -1, 0).
items.s: The products of matching coordinates are 2 and -2, whose total is 0.

items.q: Given A = [[3, -6], [4, 3]] and B = [[6, -4], [-6, 2]], find the entry in row 1 and column 2 of AB.
items.s: Row 1 of A is (3, -6) and column 2 of B is (-4, 2), so the entry is 3 x -4 + -6 x 2 = -24.

items.q: Given A = [[-5, 6, -1], [-3, 1, -3]], find the entry in row 1 and column 2 of the transpose of A.
items.s: The transpose writes rows as columns, so this entry is the one in row 2 and column 1 of A, namely -3.

items.q: Given A = [[-6, 0], [-6, 8]] and I the identity array of order two, find the top left entry of A + 2 I.
items.s: Scaling the identity changes only the diagonal, so the top left entry is -6 + 2 = -4.
The product is diagonal with entries 27, 14 and 9, so its trace is 50.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[4, -1], [6, 5]].
items.s: For an array of order two the number is (4)(5) - (-1)(6) = 26.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[4, 4, 2], [0, 4, 0], [0, 2, 1]].
items.s: Expanding along the first column leaves 4 times the order two number 4 x 1, giving 16.

items.q: An array A of order two has determinant 4. Find the determinant of 2A.
items.s: Scaling both rows multiplies the number by 2^2 = 4, so the answer is 4 x 4 = 16.

items.q: Find the determinant of the upper triangular array [[6, 7, 2], [0, 4, 5], [0, 0, 5]].
items.s: For a triangular array the number is the product of the diagonal entries, here 6 x 4 x 5 = 120.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[2, 3, 3], [3, 3, 5], [0, 0, 0]].
items.s: The last row is entirely zero, so expanding along it gives a total of 0.

items.q: Find the top left entry of the inverse of [[4, 3], [2, 2]].
items.s: The determinant is 2, and the top left entry of the undoing array is 2/2 = 1.

items.q: Find the bottom left entry of the inverse of [[4, 3], [1, 6]].
items.s: The bottom left entry of the undoing array is minus the lower left entry divided by the determinant 21, giving -0.0476.

items.q: A system with coefficient array [[1, 4], [2, 4]] has right hand column (3, 9). Using the determinant method, find the first unknown.
items.s: The first unknown is (3 x 4 - 4 x 9)/-4 = 6.

items.q: The system 2x + 3y = 4 and 2x + 2y = 7 has coefficient array [[2, 3], [2, 2]]. State the number of solutions it has.
items.s: The determinant of the coefficient array is -2, which is nonzero, so the system has exactly one solution = 1.

items.q: Solve the system 2x + 1y = 11 and 1x + 3y = 18. State the value of y.
items.s: The determinant of the coefficient array is 5, and solving gives x = 3 and y = 5, so the value asked for is 5.

items.q: The reduced form of an array with 4 rows and five columns has 2 rows that are not entirely zero, all the other rows being zero. State its rank.
items.s: The rank is the count of rows that are not entirely zero in the reduced form, which is 2.

items.q: An array has 4 columns and its reduced form has 1 rows that are not entirely zero. State its nullity.
items.s: Nullity is the count of columns without a leading entry, that is 4 - 1 = 3.

items.q: An array has 4 rows and 5 columns. State the largest value its rank can take.
items.s: The rank cannot exceed the smaller of the two counts, which here is 4.

items.q: State the dimension of the space of all arrays with 3 rows and 4 columns under the usual entry by entry operations.
items.s: Every entry may be chosen freely, so the dimension is 3 x 4 = 12.

items.q: Two members of the plane have coordinates (2, 1) and (4, 2). State 1 if they are independent and 0 if they are dependent.
items.s: The second member is 2 times the first, so the pair is dependent and the answer is 0.

items.q: An array of order two has eigenvalues 4 and 6. State its trace.
items.s: The trace equals the total of the eigenvalues, which is 10.

items.q: An array of order two has eigenvalues 4 and 3. State its determinant.
items.s: The determinant equals the product of the eigenvalues, which is 12.

items.q: The characteristic expression of an array of order two is L^2 - 7L + 12, where L stands for the unknown number. State the smaller of the two values it produces when set to zero.
items.s: The expression has roots 3 and 4, so the smaller is 3.

items.q: Find the product of the two eigenvalues of [[-1, -2], [0, -3]].
items.s: The product of the eigenvalues equals the determinant, which is (-1)(-3) - (-2)(0) = 3.

items.q: Three of these relate to Rank and echelon form. Which one does not?
o: unique solution
reduced row echelon form
row echelon form
rank
items.s: Every other option belongs to Rank and echelon form. “unique solution” belongs to Systems of linear equations, not Rank and echelon form.

items.q: In this course, eigenvector refers to
o: a number for which some nonzero member is carried to a multiple of itself
a nonzero member that a given array merely stretches or reverses
the whole collection of values attached to an array
how many times a value appears as a root of the expression in a single symbol
items.s: eigenvector: a nonzero member that a given array merely stretches or reverses. The other options describe eigenvalue, spectrum, algebraic multiplicity.

items.q: In this course, orthogonal matrix refers to
o: the array of signed smaller values of a square one, written with rows and columns interchanged
a square one that is its own undoing array
a square one whose rows and columns interchanged array is also its undoing array
the array which, multiplied by the given one on either side, gives the identity
items.s: orthogonal matrix: a square one whose rows and columns interchanged array is also its undoing array. The other options describe adjugate, inverse, involutory matrix.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains singular matrix.
o: a square one in which every entry on one side of the leading diagonal is zero
a square one whose attached single number is zero
the writing of the whole number as a sum of entries of one row each multiplied by its signed smaller value
the situation in which two rows of a square array are equal so that its number is zero
items.s: singular matrix: a square one whose attached single number is zero. The other options describe vanishing row case, cofactor expansion, triangular matrix.

items.q: In this course, orthogonal complement refers to
o: everything that is assigned the number zero with every member of a stated part
a rule assigning a number to each ordered pair of members, symmetric and positive on each member with itself
the statement that the assigned number of a pair never exceeds the product of the two lengths
two members whose assigned number under the pairing rule is zero
items.s: orthogonal complement: everything that is assigned the number zero with every member of a stated part. The other options describe orthogonal members, inner product, Cauchy inequality.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an array with the same count of rows as of columns”
o: null matrix
transpose
square matrix
conformable pair
items.s: square matrix is an array with the same count of rows as of columns.

items.q: “a simplified array in which each leading entry lies to the right of the one above it” is the definition of
o: column space
row echelon form
rank
nullity
items.s: row echelon form is a simplified array in which each leading entry lies to the right of the one above it.

items.q: “a square one that becomes the negative of itself when its rows and columns are interchanged” is the definition of
o: symmetric matrix
null matrix
identity matrix
skew symmetric matrix
items.s: skew symmetric matrix is a square one that becomes the negative of itself when its rows and columns are interchanged.

items.q: “a square one whose entries away from the leading diagonal are all zero” is the definition of
o: conformable pair
null matrix
symmetric matrix
diagonal matrix
items.s: diagonal matrix is a square one whose entries away from the leading diagonal are all zero.
